domain: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions - Resilient Architectures
vignette: An international fintech institution hosts an automated foreign exchange settlement API across two AWS Regions: us-east-1 (primary) and us-west-2 (disaster recovery). The workload's compute layer is deployed on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs), persisting state to a multi-AZ Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. During a simulated regional outage of us-east-1, the architecture failed its business continuity audit: client traffic took up to 12 minutes to reroute due to downstream corporate resolver caching of Amazon Route 53 DNS records, violating the mandatory Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 60 seconds. Furthermore, the data layer sustained 45 seconds of transactional discrepancy before database promotion completed, breaching the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 5 seconds. A Solutions Architect must re-architect the solution to achieve automated regional failover within the 60-second RTO, maintain an RPO under 5 seconds, and eliminate client resolver caching latency.
question: Which architecture meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.A: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator with two dual-stack Anycast IP addresses, configuring endpoint groups for the ALBs in us-east-1 and us-west-2 with continuous TCP health checks. Convert the Aurora database into an Amazon Aurora Global Database spanning us-east-1 and us-west-2 with physical storage-level replication. Use Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal and regional routing controls with AWS Lambda automation to initiate managed unplanned failover of the Aurora Global Database during primary failure.
options.B: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of both regional ALBs with an origin group configuring primary and secondary origins for automated 502/503 failover. Migrate the persistence layer from Aurora PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables with multi-region active-active replication to achieve continuous millisecond RPO and immediate failover.
options.C: Configure Amazon Route 53 with multi-value answer routing and lower the Time to Live (TTL) of the API endpoint record to 1 second. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with Change Data Capture (CDC) to stream continuous writes from the primary Aurora cluster in us-east-1 to a read-replica Aurora cluster in us-west-2, automating promotion via AWS Step Functions.
options.D: Provision an AWS Transit Gateway multi-region peering connection between us-east-1 and us-west-2. Deploy Network Load Balancers (NLBs) routing traffic across regions through the Transit Gateway. Configure Aurora PostgreSQL with asynchronous logical cross-region read replication and write-forwarding enabled on the secondary replica.
options.high_yield_pearl: AWS Global Accelerator eliminates DNS caching latency by utilizing static Anycast IP addresses routed across the AWS global backbone, achieving failover within seconds (<30s). Paired with Amazon Aurora Global Database (storage-level physical replication with typical lag <1s), this is the definitive AWS reference pattern for sub-minute RTO and sub-5-second RPO multi-region architectures.
options.tactics_and_technique: Apply the 3-step elimination heuristic for Multi-Region AWS DR questions: 1. Evaluate Routing Mechanism: If the vignette cites client-side/ISP DNS resolver caching or strict <60s RTO, eliminate all DNS-based solutions (Route 53 TTL reductions fail because client/ISP resolvers frequently enforce a minimum TTL floor, making Option C incorrect). CloudFront origin groups (Option B) handle read/cache workloads well but lack fine-grained transactional API failover and force a drastic NoSQL migration from relational PostgreSQL. 2. Evaluate Data Layer RPO: AWS DMS CDC (Option C) and logical replication (Option D) introduce network/compute overhead that routinely exceeds strict 5-second RPOs under peak write loads, whereas Aurora Global Database uses dedicated storage-layer physical replication directly on the NVMe/EBS storage tier without compute bottlenecks (<1 second lag). 3. Confirm ARC Control: Route 53 Application Recovery Controller provides deterministic execution without split-brain risk, satisfying RTO < 60s and RPO < 5s.
